quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
A curve in the road ahead.
Changes in traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes caused by drunk driving?

options.text: Decide before drinking that you will not drive.
Tell someone, "No thanks, I'm driving," if they offer you a drink.
Call a taxi.
Do any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do any of the above.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving crashes is to decide before drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it is harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. Wait until the gate is raised and you can see clearly in both directions before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and go find help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. Rescuers are more likely to find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. Rescuers are more likely to find you there.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are easier to find in your vehicle. Walking in a snowstorm can be dangerous.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look in the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn drivers about railroad crossings. You must yield to trains and not try to go around them.

questions.question: When entering a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.question: A sign says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before reaching the reduced speed zone.
You should reduce your speed to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A reduced speed sign tells drivers to slow down. The new speed limit shown begins at that sign.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield
Do not enter

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a yield sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and cross traffic go first. Only stop if necessary.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: You must use low beams when you are:

options.text: On a lighted street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: A vehicle is entering your freeway lane from an entrance ramp. You should:

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Honk your horn so they know you are there.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.
Change lanes to allow them room, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to allow them room, if possible.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the freeway. Change lanes when you can to help them merge safely.

questions.question: You find a defect that may affect your vehicle's safe operation. You should:

options.text: Correct the defect as soon as possible.
Correct the defect when you can afford it.
Drive the vehicle at slower speeds.
Drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Correct the defect as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: Fix any defect that affects safe operation right away. Do not drive the vehicle until the defect is repaired.

questions.question: You should not use your horn:

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may confuse or startle them. Yield to them and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: The road has one solid yellow line and one broken yellow line in the center. If the broken line is next to your lane, it means:

options.text: You are not allowed to pass in this area.
You are in a passing zone and it is safe for you to pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in a passing zone and it is safe for you to pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass. A solid yellow line on the other side means oncoming traffic cannot pass.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking downhill with or without a curb, turn your wheels right toward the road edge. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road with a curb, turn your wheels left toward the center so the vehicle rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Divided highway begins.
A steep grade is ahead.
The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are about to merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has a low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an overpass ahead is low. Do not drive under it if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign.

questions.question: To be ready for hazards ahead, you should:

options.text: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.
Maintain focus toward the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.
questions.explanation: Look ahead and spot problems before you reach them. Do not just look at the center of the road. Scan the whole road and both sides to stay safe.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone, you should:

options.text: Slightly increase your speed.
Expect the unexpected.
Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect the unexpected.
questions.explanation: Conditions in construction zones can change quickly and unexpectedly. Drive with extra caution to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. You should:

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on your emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold your steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly after a blowout. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Release the accelerator and slow down gradually. Once you are going very slowly, apply the brakes lightly and pull to a safe area off the road.
